practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient instance (process-wide singleton) rather than opening/closing clients per request, and await a single client.connect() promise at startup.
practices.prior_belief: Reuse a single MongoClient instance across the Node.js process, configure a connection pool (maxPoolSize) appropriate to concurrency, and set sensible timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS and socketTimeoutMS) rather than opening/closing clients per request.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool and timeout settings to match the runtime (serverless: small pools, short maxIdleTimeMS; long-running servers: larger maxPoolSize and longer maxIdleTimeMS) and set retryReads/retryWrites and sensible serverSelection/socket timeouts.
Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable at runtime (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit credentials to source; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
practices.prior_belief: Read the cluster connection string from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime and never commit credentials to the repo; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.

practices.practice: Enforce TLS for all client connections and restrict network access to the cluster using firewall rules, Private Link (private endpoints) or VNet integration; avoid disabling certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Use TLS/SSL for connections and restrict network access to the cluster (IP firewall, VNet, or private endpoints); do not send credentials over plaintext or expose the cluster publicly.

practices.practice: Create a composite unique index on (customerId, eventId) so duplicate events are rejected at write time, and name it so you can manage it reliably.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound unique index on (customerId, eventId) with unique:true to deduplicate events at write time; create the index idempotently at startup (createIndexes) or via setup script so repeated runs do not fail.

practices.practice: Make index and collection setup idempotent in a bootstrap step (scripts or startup code) so repeated runs check for and create only missing indexes/collections instead of failing.
practices.prior_belief: Make index creation and collection setup part of an idempotent bootstrap step (scripts or startup code) that checks for existing indexes/collections and only creates missing ones rather than failing if run multiple times.

practices.practice: For high-throughput ingestion set bulk writes to unordered (ordered:false) to maximize throughput and treat duplicate-key errors (11000) as expected individual failures rather than aborting the whole batch.
practices.prior_belief: For high-throughput ingestion use unordered bulkWrite (ordered:false) and process BulkWriteError/writeErrors — treat duplicate-key errors (code 11000) as expected and continue without aborting the whole batch.

practices.practice: Limit per-process batch sizes for bulk writes (tune around ~1,000 documents per process/thread as a sensible starting point) and observe service limits (Azure DocumentDB supports up to 25,000 writes per single request), tuning experimentally for document size and cluster capacity.
practices.source_name: Optimize write performance in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
practices.how_found: optimize write performance Azure DocumentDB MongoDB tune batch size

practices.practice: Design ingestion idempotently by including an application-level unique eventId (and a deduplication unique index) so retries don't create duplicate logical events.
practices.prior_belief: Make ingestion idempotent: include an application-level unique eventId and rely on the unique index for deduplication rather than trying to rely on retries to preserve idempotency.

practices.practice: Use upsert (updateOne/replaceOne with upsert:true) where appropriate for idempotent writes, but use it judiciously in high-throughput paths because upserts have different performance and index impacts than simple inserts.
practices.prior_belief: Use upsert judiciously for dedup/write-if-not-exists scenarios (e.g., replaceOne with upsert:false when using unique index) instead of complex transactions if throughput is required.
practices.source_name: Manage a document in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB using JavaScript

practices.practice: Prioritize single-document writes and idempotent design for high-throughput ingestion; explicit multi-document transactions exist but do not provide a throughput advantage and can add latency and contention (no Azure DocumentDB docs recommend multi-document transactions for high-throughput ingestion).
practices.prior_belief: Don't rely on multi-document transactions for high-throughput event ingestion—prefer single-document writes or bulk unordered writes and idempotent design to maximize throughput and reduce latency.

practices.practice: Persist and periodically checkpoint change-stream resume tokens (the event _id) so a consumer can resume after crashes; use resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime to continue a stream from the last processed event.
practices.prior_belief: When using change streams, persist and periodically checkpoint resume tokens (or resumeAfter) so the consumer can resume after crashes; implement exponential backoff and reopen streams on transient errors.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB change streams resume token

practices.practice: Open change streams with an appropriate pipeline and options (e.g., fullDocument:'updateLookup', resumeAfter/startAtOperationTime) and monitor for resumability and non-resumable errors; treat change streams as long-lived cursors and implement backoff/retry on transient errors.
practices.prior_belief: Open change streams with an appropriate pipeline and maxAwaitTimeMS, and monitor for resumability errors; treat change-streams as long-lived cursors and guard against idle timeouts by handling resumable/non-resumable errors.

practices.practice: When scaling change-stream consumption, parallelize by obtaining per-physical-partition resume tokens (GetChangeStreamTokens) and run a watcher per token so streams are balanced across physical partitions.
practices.source_name: Use MongoDB extension commands to manage data stored in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

practices.practice: If change-stream tests time out, verify cluster-level support and account roles/permissions and server version for change streams before assuming application bug; add diagnostic logs and short-lived test streams to capture resume tokens.
practices.prior_belief: If change-stream tests time out, verify cluster-level support and permissions for change streams (MongoDB feature level, wire protocol version, and account roles) before assuming application bug; add diagnostic logging and short-lived test streams with immediate resume token capture.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs, and alert on cluster-level saturation metrics (CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, connection count) appropriate to the chosen compute tier.
practices.prior_belief: Emit application metrics around bulkWrite throughput, bulk write error rates (duplicate-key counts), change-stream lag, and connection pool utilization; wire these to a monitoring system and alert on increased throttling or change-stream disconnects.

practices.practice: Profile slow queries with explain('executionStats'), verify index usage and index intersections, and add projections to return only needed fields to reduce I/O.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor and profile queries: capture slow operations, use explain() for queries to verify index usage (index intersection or covered queries), and add projections to return only necessary fields.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes on a timestamp field (createIndex with expireAfterSeconds) for ephemeral event data to bound storage growth for high-volume event streams.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral event data you only need for a bounded period (createIndex({eventTimestamp:1}, {expireAfterSeconds: N})) to bound storage growth for high-volume event streams.

practices.practice: When using vector search, store normalized vectors with a fixed dimension and create a vector index using the cluster-supported sub-type (prefer DiskANN for large scale, HNSW/IVF for smaller) and tune build/search parameters for latency/recall tradeoffs.
practices.prior_belief: For deployments with vector search enabled, store normalized float vectors in a fixed-dimension field and create the vector index with the cluster's supported index type (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN) and correct dimension and metric; tune index parameters (efConstruction, M) and search ef/nearK for latency/recall tradeoffs.

practices.practice: On transient write or rate-limit errors implement idempotent retries with exponential backoff and jitter, and ensure your deduplication key prevents duplicate logical events when retries succeed.
practices.prior_belief: When retrying write operations on transient errors, use idempotent retry semantics (exponential backoff, jitter) and ensure deduplication key (customerId + eventId) prevents duplicate logical events from being applied twice.

practices.practice: Do not assume Azure DocumentDB uses the Cosmos DB 'RU' provisioning model; Azure DocumentDB uses selectable compute tiers and independently sized storage (vCores/tiers), so plan capacity by picking an appropriate cluster tier, storage and sharding approach rather than only thinking in RUs.
practices.prior_belief: Provision throughput appropriately for sustained ingestion: either provision collection/database throughput or use autoscale if available; monitor RU consumption (or equivalent) and scale before throttling becomes frequent.

practices.practice: Avoid creating many large or wide compound indexes that include low-selectivity fields; keep an index budget (review $indexStats) and remove or hide unused indexes to reduce write amplification during heavy ingestion.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid creating many large or wide compound indexes that include low-selectivity fields; design indexes to support actual query patterns (filter -> sort -> projection) and remove unused indexes during heavy ingestion to reduce write amplification.

practices.practice: Examine BulkWriteResult/writeErrors on partial bulk failures and retry only the failed operations that are retryable (do not blindly re-run entire batches), treating duplicate-key errors as non-retryable logical duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Handle partial bulk failures by examining BulkWriteResult and writeErrors: retry only the failed operations that are retryable (not duplicate-key) and do not blindly re-run entire batches.
practices.source_name: Perform bulk operations on Azure Cosmos DB data

practices.practice: Use least privilege for application access: prefer Microsoft Entra ID / managed identities with RBAC for service authentication, create per-app secondary users if needed, and rotate any long-lived credentials regularly.
practices.prior_belief: Ensure proper IAM/role management: grant least privilege to the ingestion service (only insert/replace/find privileges on the target DB/collection) and rotate any long-lived keys regularly.

practices.practice: Make event documents small (stay well under the 16 MB BSON limit); if events can include large binary or high-cardinality payloads, store those blobs in object storage and keep a reference in the document.
practices.prior_belief: Keep event documents small (avoid embedding large binary payloads) and store large payloads in object storage with a reference in the event document when size could approach document limits.

practices.practice: Make index creation part of an idempotent bootstrap (script or startup) that checks for existing indexes and only creates missing ones rather than failing if run multiple times.
Normalize the approach to retries and backoff in client code: implement exponential backoff with jitter and respect server retry-after headers for rate-limited responses.

Azure DocumentDB exposes MongoDB change streams as the recommended change feed mechanism for MongoDB-compatible workloads; there is not a separate Cosmos DB change-feed alternative to prefer for this API.
practices.prior_belief: If the managed service exposes a platform-native change feed (e.g., Cosmos DB Change Feed), evaluate using that instead of MongoDB change streams if it offers better SLAs/availability or integrates better with Azure tooling.
